newsitem.title: USA: Fannie Mae April net portfolio up $3.7 bln.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae April net portfolio up $3.7 bln.

text.p: Fannie Mae said Monday that its net mortgage portfolio grew by $3.7 billion in April to $295.1 billion.
On an annualized basis, growth in April was at a rate of 15.1 percent, up from 13.4 percent in March.
Fannie Mae said mortgage purchases were $6.7 billion in April, up from $5.8 billion in March, while portfolio liquidations stood at $3.0 billion last month compared with $2.7 billion in March.
Net commitments to purchase mortgages were $3.9 billion in April compared with $8.3 billion in March, it said.

Fannie Mae said its total net interest margin rose one basis point to 117 basis points, also reflecting a matching increase in the portfolio net interest margin to 131 basis points and a higher return on the mortgage-backed securities (MBS) float.

Total MBS outstanding rose $2.9 billion last month to $666.6 billion, a 5.3 percent annual growth rate, it said. MBS issues were $9.5 billion in April compared with $10 billion in March, while MBS April liquidations stood at $6.5 billion compared with $5.5 billion the previous month.

Fannie Mae said the conventional single-family at-risk serious delinquency rate declined to 0.59 percent in March from 0.60 percent in February. It said the conventional multifamily at-risk serious delinquency rate was 0.58 percent in March compared with a February rate of 0.56 percent.
